note: Two primitive camping areas in the Missouri River bottoms, each a small gravel parking lot in young bottomland timber with no pads, tables or privy: one beside Riverbottom Road about 0.4 mile inside the area, the other at the end of a short gravel spur east of the road. The way in is gravel from the end of Route Y's pavement, over a railroad crossing; the whole area is floodplain behind the levee. The river is half a mile or more from either lot, beyond the levee. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: MDC 'Designated Camping Sites' - two Primitive Camping Area symbols on the map, each beside a parking-lot symbol, and two GIS camping points. Free, FCFS, no hookups, 14-day limit; the brochure says camping is allowed anytime, with no amenities. No waterfowl zone or refuge on the map. Pin is in timber 103 m from its lot: move to the lot. Stored phone differs from the area page.
flags: INCLUSION (lot rule - stays, but thin): the area page lists 'Camping: Designated Camping Sites' (and 'Boat-in along Missouri River'); the brochure says 'Camping is allowed anytime in designated camping areas shown on map. These may or may not have defined campsites. No amenities are provided.' The map (03/10) draws two Primitive Camping Area symbols, each directly beside a Parking Lot symbol: one on Riverbottom Rd, one at the end of a gravel spur to the east. GIS layer 27 has two 'Primitive Camping Area' points (OBJECTIDs 403, 404), each about 100 m from its lot in planted timber. On the 160 m leaf-off frame each lot is a bare gravel pad with nothing else: the spur-end lot about 15 x 25 m, the roadside one about 15 x 12 m with a vehicle parked on the road beside it. No pads, loop, privy or fire rings are visible at either, and nothing but young trees at the GIS points themselves. MDC designates a camping point at each lot, so under the 2026-11-09 rule it stays; in practice a rig camps on the lot. A 23-ft rig fits the spur-end lot; the roadside lot is tighter.

PIN MOVE: stored 38.80619,-92.41028 is GIS point 404, in closed-canopy timber 103 m north of the lot it belongs to. Move to the gravel lot at the end of the spur, 38.80529,-92.41045 (seen on the leaf-off frame; GIS lot 862 is at 38.80527,-92.41045). The other camping lot is at 38.81197,-92.41450 (GIS lot 861), 760 m north-west on the same road - one entrance, no split. Neither is plainly the main camp.

ACCESS: 'take Route Y north 5 miles to end of pavement, continue on Riverbottom Road east 0.50 mile crossing railroad tracks to area.' The map legend shows Riverbottom Rd and the spur as Gravel Road and the rest as levee and area access trails. No ford, low-water crossing, 4WD wording or posted limit on the page, brochure or map. It is river bottom land behind a levee, so high water will close it. OSM was unread (the Overpass mirror did not answer).
PHONE: stored 573-796-0286 does not match the area page, which says 'For more information call (573) 815-7900'. Suggest 573-815-7900.

WATERFRONT: stored not waterfront stands - both lots are inland in timber, by the area map scale the river is about half a mile north of the roadside lot and over a mile east of the spur-end lot, beyond the levee.
